selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 8552, the Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2026, directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to increase the rates of disability compensation for veterans with service-connected disabilities and the rates of dependency and indemnity compensation for eligible survivors, effective December 1, 2026.

affected_groups.effect: Receive an increase in their monthly disability compensation rates and clothing allowances.
Receive an increase in dependency and indemnity compensation for surviving spouses and children.

key_provisions: Increases wartime disability compensation, additional compensation for dependents, and clothing allowance rates starting December 1, 2026.
Increases dependency and indemnity compensation rates for surviving spouses and children starting December 1, 2026.
Sets the percentage of the increase to match the Social Security benefit increase determined under section 215(i) of the Social Security Act.
Allows the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to make administrative adjustments to certain other compensation rates.
Requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to publish the newly adjusted rates in the Federal Register.
missing_information: The specific percentage amount of the increase, as it depends on future Social Security determinations.
The total monetary cost of the adjustments.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 8552, the Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2026, directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to increase the rates of disability compensation for veterans with service-connected disabilities and the rates of dependency and indemnity compensation for eligible survivors, effective December 1, 2026.
summary_detail.significance: The bill provides a cost-of-living increase to benefits for disabled veterans and their survivors, aligning the adjustment percentage with changes in Social Security benefits.
